note: Events of the island game (Phase 2): campaigns, sieges, supply, plague, mercenaries, embassies, Sicels and Italian Greeks, Carthage's council and its houses, and towns changing sides. Same shape as data/events.json, plus 'places' (the towns an event is about), parts played by the generated cast ('census') or Carthage's named men ('punic'), and an 'island' block in 'when' for cities, armies and Carthage. History comes in as conditions, never dates (design council V8). They fire only in island games, from their own draw each season. The engine is src/core/events.ts with src/core/island-events.ts; the research card is docs/research/island-events.md.

events.name: A gate at midnight
events.text: A man comes to your tent by night from {town}. {Traitor}, who leads the town, will open a gate to you at midnight, for great promises and the safety of his kin.
events.why: your army is before {town}, and {traitor} sees how the siege will end

choices.label: Pay what he asks

success.text: At midnight a gate swings open. Your men are inside before the watch can cry out.

failure.text: The plot is found out. {Traitor}'s head is shown on the walls at dawn, and your silver is gone.

effects.why: they caught a traitor in your pay

choices.label: Promise him that he will rule {town} for you

success.text: {Traitor} takes your word. The gate opens, and he rules {town} in your name.

effects.why: one of their own still rules them

failure.text: {Traitor} wanted silver, not promises. No gate opens.

choices.label: Take no town by treachery

effects.why: the soldiers wanted the easy way in

facts.text: Catana was betrayed to Dionysius by its general, who let him in about midnight.
facts.quote: the general of the Catanians, had offered to betray the city to him. Consequently, being admitted by

facts.text: Naxos was handed over by its commander, won over by great promises.
facts.quote: Procles, the commander of the Naxians, on being won over by great promises, delivered over his native city to Dionysius

invented: the traitor is the town's first man from the generated cast

events.name: The mole to the island
events.text: Motya stands on an island off the shore, and its people have broken the narrow causeway so that no enemy can come at their walls. Your engineers say the strait can be filled, if enough men carry earth and stone.
events.why: your army is before Motya, and the causeway is cut

choices.label: Fill the strait and build a mole
choices.text: Thousands carry stone. Little by little the mole runs out toward the walls, and the engines go forward with it.

choices.label: Ring it with ships and starve it
Attack it as it stands

facts.text: Motya lay on an island six stades off Sicily; its people breached the causeway.
facts.quote: It also had a narrow artificial causeway extending to the shore of Sicily, which the Motyans breached at this time

facts.text: Dionysius filled the strait and advanced his engines along the mole.
facts.quote: he at once put many times more men on the task of filling up the strait between the city and the coast, and, as the mole was extended, advanced his engines of war little by little toward the walls

events.name: Towers six storeys high
events.text: The siege of {town} drags on. Your engineers want to build wheeled towers as tall as the houses, bring up the rams, and keep the battlements clear with catapults.
events.why: your army has sat before {town} for a season

choices.label: Bring up towers, rams and catapults
choices.text: The towers roll forward and the rams hammer the walls of {town}.

effects.why: the rams break a stretch of wall

choices.label: Build rams and sheds with what you have
Wait for hunger to do the work

events.note: The towers need the arms workshops (the event of that name) to have been set up.

facts.text: At Motya Dionysius used rams, catapults and wheeled towers six stories high.
facts.quote: kept hammering the towers with his battering-rams, while with the catapults he kept down the fighters on the battlements; and he also advanced against the walls his wheeled towers, six stories high

invented: trigger (any town with walls you have besieged for a season)

events.name: Heralds to the temples
events.text: Your army has burst into {town}. The Sicilian Greeks remember what Carthage did to their own cities and kill everyone they meet, sparing neither child nor old man.
events.why: you took {town}, a town of Carthage's own

choices.label: Send heralds to cry: take refuge in the Greek temples
choices.text: The heralds cry it in every street. Those who reach the temples live, to be sold.

choices.label: Let the soldiers have their way
Stop the killing with your own guard

success.text: Your guard stands between the soldiers and the townspeople. The killing stops.

failure.text: No one listens. The killing goes on until it burns itself out.

effects.why: you set the guard against the army

facts.text: At Motya the Sicilian Greeks slew everyone they met.
facts.quote: for the Sicilian Greeks, eager to return cruelty for cruelty, slew everyone they encountered, sparing without distinction not a child, not a woman, not an elder

facts.text: Dionysius, wanting captives to sell, sent heralds telling the Motyans to flee to the Greek temples.
facts.quote: he stationed heralds to cry aloud and tell the Motyans to take refuge in the temples which were revered by the Greeks

invented: trigger (taking a town of Carthage's own)

events.name: Greeks who fought for Carthage
events.text: Among the captives at {town} are Greeks who fought on Carthage's side, and were taken with weapons in their hands.
events.why: you took {town}, and Greeks were among its defenders

choices.label: Crucify them, as a lesson

effects.why: they heard what you did to Greeks who sided with Carthage

choices.label: Enlist them in your guard

effects.why: hardened men who know Carthage's ways

choices.label: Send them home

facts.text: After Motya Dionysius crucified Daimenes and other Greeks who had fought for Carthage.
facts.quote: and other Greeks who had fought on the side of the Carthaginians and had been taken captive

events.name: The first man on the wall
events.text: {Town} is yours. The soldiers say that {hero} was the first man to climb its wall, and they wait to see how you reward courage.

choices.label: Reward {hero} with silver and honour the brave
Give him a crown of olive before the army

effects.why: a hired captain honoured above citizens

choices.label: Courage is what you pay them for

effects.why: no reward for the first man on the wall

facts.text: Dionysius rewarded Archylus, the first up the wall of Motya, with one hundred minas, and honoured the brave.
facts.quote: he rewarded Archylus, who had been the first to mount the wall, with one hundred minas, and honoured according to their merits all others who had performed deeds of valour

invented: the hero is one of your hired captains from the generated cast (the source names Archylus of Thurii)

events.name: Ships on the beach
events.text: Your warships lie hauled up on the beach before {town}. At dawn Carthage's best ships appear off the harbour mouth, hoping to catch them on land and break the siege.
events.why: Carthage holds the sea, and your fleet is beached at {town}

choices.label: Haul the ships over land to open sea, and man them with archers
choices.text: The soldiers drag the ships across the land. Archers and slingers on the decks, and catapults on the shore, drive the enemy off.

choices.label: Fight them at the harbour mouth

success.text: The enemy is caught in the narrows and beaten.

failure.text: Your ships are rammed as they come out, one by one.

choices.label: Lift the siege to save the ships

effects.why: you would not lose the fleet

facts.text: Himilcon came with his hundred best triremes to catch Dionysius' ships hauled up in the harbour of Motya.
facts.quote: hearing that Dionysius had hauled his warships up on land, manned at once his hundred best triremes

facts.text: Dionysius hauled the ships over land, manned them with archers and slingers, and used the new catapults from the shore.
facts.quote: he hauled his vessels over the land with no difficulty and launched them safely in the sea outside the harbour

invented: trigger (any port your army besieges while Carthage has a fleet)

events.name: The baggage is late
events.text: The mule train has not come up, and the last of the bread is in the soldiers' packs. The quartermasters ask what the army is to eat.
events.why: your army is in enemy land with little food

choices.label: Send out foragers in strength

mods.label: it is summer, and the fields are full
it is winter, and the fields are bare

success.text: The foragers come back with grain and cattle.

failure.text: The foragers are caught scattered in the fields and cut down.

choices.label: Buy grain from {near}

effects.why: you paid well for their grain

choices.label: Kill the baggage animals and eat them

effects.why: the levies grumble at eating mules

choices.label: March on and hope

events.name: Cut off their foragers
events.text: Carthage's army is in hostile country and short of food. Its foragers go out every day in long, careless columns.
events.why: Carthage's army has little food and is far from its own towns

choices.label: Send horsemen to ambush the foragers

success.text: Your horsemen fall on the foragers again and again. Carthage's army goes hungry.

failure.text: The foragers were bait. Your horsemen ride into the enemy's cavalry.

choices.label: Pay the men of {town}, who know the ground, to harry them
Let hunger do its own work

facts.text: Magon, camped in hostile land and short of supplies, was harried by Agyris' troops, who knew the ground.
facts.quote: the troops of Agyris, being familiar with the territory, held the advantage in laying ambushes and were continually cutting off the enemy's supplies

invented: local men from one of the island's towns play the part of Agyris' troops

events.name: The grain convoy
events.text: Syracuse is besieged and the granaries are low. Merchant ships with grain from Sardinia and Libya are waiting offshore for an escort past Carthage's fleet.
events.why: Carthage besieges Syracuse, and you have little grain

choices.label: Sail out yourself to escort the grain

success.text: You bring the grain ships in. While you were at sea the citizens sailed out on their own, took a Punic food ship, and are proud of it.

effects.why: they fought and won without you

failure.text: The convoy is scattered. You come back with half of it.

choices.label: Send {admiral} with the fleet

failure.text: Carthage's ships catch the convoy. Grain and warships go to the bottom.

choices.label: Ration what is left

effects.why: short rations in a besieged city

facts.text: Besieged, Dionysius sent merchant ships to Sardinia and Libya for grain.
facts.quote: He also dispatched merchant ships to Sardinia and Libya to secure grain and every kind of food

facts.text: While Dionysius and Leptines escorted supplies, the Syracusans on their own took a food ship.
facts.quote: Dionysius and Leptines had set out with warships to escort a supply of provisions; and the Syracusans, who were thus left to themselves

events.name: Fever in the lines
events.text: The summer is hot and the camp before {town} is crowded. Men in the lowest lines are falling sick, and the physicians blame the bad water and the ground.
events.why: a crowded camp in the hot months before {town}

choices.label: Move the camp to higher ground

effects.why: you gave up the lowest lines

choices.label: Burn the dead and keep the lines
Lift the siege before it spreads

events.note: The causes the physicians name follow Diodorus 14.70.4 to 14.70.5 (crowding, the season, the water, marshy ground), but this event is invention.

events.name: Plague in the Punic camp
events.text: Plague has struck Carthage's camp before {town}. It took the Libyans first. Now the dead lie unburied, and no one dares go near the sick.
events.why: a crowded camp in the hot months, and, the priests say, the gods' anger

choices.label: Attack by land and sea at dawn

mods.label: your army is in the field

success.text: Your army comes round by night and falls on the camp at daybreak while your ships burn theirs at anchor.

failure.text: Even sick men fight hard behind a rampart. Your attack is thrown back.

choices.label: Let the plague do its work

facts.text: A plague struck the Carthaginian army before Syracuse, from crowding, the season and the heat.
facts.quote: that myriads of people were gathered together, that it was the time of year which is most productive of plagues

facts.text: The camp's ground was marshy and in a hollow.
facts.quote: since the terrain was marshy and in a hollow

facts.text: The plague first attacked the Libyans; soon no one dared approach the sick.
facts.quote: Now the plague first attacked the Libyans

facts.text: Dionysius attacked the camp by land and the ships by sea at daybreak.
facts.quote: ordered Pharacidas and Leptines the admirals to attack the enemy's ships at daybreak, while he himself, profiting by a moonless night, made a circuit with his army

invented: trigger (plague breaking out in a Carthaginian siege camp, from the island's own plague roll)
events.note: Diodorus also gives a religious cause, the plundered temple of Demeter and Kore (14.70.4). The game's plague comes from the camp; the event names both.

events.name: A bargain by night
events.text: Beaten and sick, {general} sends to you in secret, behind your citizens' backs. Let his own Carthaginians sail home by night, and the 300 talents in his camp are yours. His hired men and his allies he will leave behind.
events.why: {general}'s army is in a bad way, and he wants to save what he can

choices.label: Take the silver and let them go by night
choices.text: On the fourth night the Carthaginians slip away. The Iberians left behind send a herald and ask to serve you; the rest throw down their arms.

effects.why: the Iberians take service with you
fear of Carthage keeps the city close to you
Carthage keeps men to come back with

choices.label: Refuse, and finish them

success.text: Your men cut down the army as it tries to reach the ships.

failure.text: They fight their way to the shore and get away, and they owe you nothing.

facts.text: The Carthaginians, beaten, offered Dionysius three hundred talents in secret to let their troops cross to Libya.
facts.quote: they entered into negotiations with Dionysius without the knowledge of the Syracusans. They asked him to allow their remaining troops to cross back to Libya and promised to give him the three hundred talents

facts.text: Diodorus says Dionysius agreed so that fear of Carthage would keep the Syracusans from seeking their freedom.
facts.quote: in order that the Syracusans, by reason of their fear of the Carthaginians, should never find a time of ease to assert their freedom

facts.text: The Iberians left behind took service with Dionysius.
facts.quote: Dionysius made peace with the Iberians and enrolled them in his mercenaries

invented: trigger (plague, a lost battle, or a starving army)
all numbers (300 talents is shown as 4 silver)
events.note: Diodorus' reason for the deal is his own judgement of Dionysius' motive; the game shows it as the effect on plots, not as fact.

events.name: Pay in land
events.text: The mercenaries are hostile, and you fear they may depose you. They gather under arms and demand their pay, with some sharpness. Leontini's good land lies empty enough to give away.
events.why: the guard wants its pay, and you have more men than silver

choices.label: Give them the city and land of Leontini in place of pay
choices.text: The mercenaries gladly take the land and share it out in lots. You recruit new men to take their place at your door.

effects.why: many go off to farm at Leontini
Carthage sees Leontini garrisoned by your men

choices.label: Arrest {commander} and send him to Sparta for trial

effects.why: sent to Sparta to face trial

effects.reason: you arrested him and sent him to Sparta

choices.label: Pay them from the treasury
Promise pay later

facts.text: Fearing the mercenaries might depose him, Dionysius arrested their commander Aristotle.
facts.quote: seeing that the mercenaries were most hostile to him and fearing that they might depose him, first of all arrested Aristotle, their commander

facts.text: He sent Aristotle to Sparta for trial and gave the ten thousand mercenaries Leontini in place of pay.
facts.quote: offered to the mercenaries, who numbered about ten thousand, in lieu of their pay the city and territory of the Leontines

facts.text: They shared out the land and settled in Leontini; he recruited new mercenaries.
facts.quote: after portioning it out in allotments they made their home in Leontini

invented: trigger (unpaid guard, or a recent peace)
events.note: The court event 'The mercenaries' demand' tells the same story in the citadel game.

events.name: Punic silver for a captain
events.text: Your watchers report that Carthage's agents have been at {captain}'s tent, offering his men double pay to change sides.
events.why: Carthage's army is on the island, and hired men follow the higher pay

choices.label: Raise his men's pay
Pay him off and send him away before he turns

effects.why: {captain} and his men are sent away

choices.label: Let him seem to sell himself, and carry Carthage a false report

success.text: Carthage's general believes {captain}'s report and marches on a lie.

failure.text: {Captain} sells himself in earnest, and his men with him.

choices.label: Trust him

success.text: {Captain} sends Carthage's agents away with their silver.

events.name: Envoys to the Campanians
events.text: Carthage's general sends envoys to the Campanian horsemen who hold {town} for you, urging them to change sides. He promises them land and a share of the spoils, and reminds them that their kinsmen at Entella side with Carthage.

choices.label: Send them their pay early
Take their families as hostages

effects.why: you hold their wives and children

choices.label: Trust them to keep faith

success.text: The Campanians send the envoys back unheard.

facts.text: Himilcon sent envoys to the Campanians who held Aetna, urging them to revolt from Dionysius.
facts.quote: sent ambassadors to the Campanians who held

facts.text: He promised them land and spoils, and pointed to the Campanians of Entella, who sided with Carthage.
facts.quote: He promised both to give them a large amount of territory and to let them share in the spoils of the war

invented: trigger (any town of yours near Carthage's army; the source names Aetna)

events.name: The harvest is waiting
events.text: The men of {town} who march with you say their fields are ripe and their wives cannot bring in the harvest alone.
events.why: your army has been out since spring, and the grain is ripe

choices.label: Let {town}'s men go home

effects.why: {town}'s men go home for the harvest
you let their men go home

choices.label: Keep them under the standards

effects.why: their harvest rots in the fields
the harvest rots in the fields

choices.label: Pay them to stay

events.name: The goddesses' temple
events.text: Carthage's soldiers have taken the suburb of Achradina and stripped the temple of Demeter and Kore of its offerings. The city is horrified, and the priestesses say the goddesses will not forget.
events.why: Carthage's army is at the walls of Syracuse

choices.label: Proclaim the sacrilege at every altar

effects.why: the gods are on our side
word of the sacrilege reaches Carthage

choices.label: Vow a new temple to the Two Goddesses
Say nothing

facts.text: Himilcon took the suburb of Achradina and plundered the temples of Demeter and Kore.
facts.quote: he also plundered the temples of both Demeter and

facts.text: Afterwards the Carthaginians believed the gods were fighting them and voted to propitiate them.
facts.quote: Consequently they voted by every means to propitiate the gods who had been sinned against
